card.title: Snell to total internal reflection — when light refuses to leave

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Light bends toward the normal entering a denser medium, away leaving it — speed changes (v = c/μ), frequency does not. Refractive index μ = c/v = sin i/sin r (Snell). Past the critical angle going dense→rare, refraction becomes impossible and ALL light reflects: total internal reflection, the engine of fibre optics, diamonds and mirages.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Snell: μ₁·sin i = μ₂·sin r  ·  μ = c/v = λ_vacuum/λ_medium  ·  critical: sin C = 1/μ (dense→rare only)  ·  lateral shift through slab: d = t·sin(i−r)/cos r  ·  glass μ = 1.5 → v = c/1.5 = 2×10⁸ m/s

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Snell's sine form needs a single wavelength (μ varies with colour — dispersion). TIR needs BOTH denser-to-rarer travel AND i > C; miss either and ordinary partial reflection/refraction rules. Lateral shift assumes parallel slab faces and a narrow beam.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Normal incidence (i = 0) never deviates. Diamond's μ ≈ 2.4 gives C ≈ 24° — tiny critical angle, endless internal sparkle. Glass μ = 1.5 → light slows to 2×10⁸ m/s (NEB 2023). Optical fibre, endoscope and sparkling air bubbles in glass are TIR applications.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Glass μ = 1.5: speed v = c/μ = 3×10⁸/1.5 = 2×10⁸ m/s; critical angle sin C = 1/1.5 → C ≈ 41.8° (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Any ray inside glass striking the boundary above ~42° cannot escape — it totally internally reflects.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Snell with one μ blurs for white light (each colour has its own μ — hence dispersion, next unit). The 'critical angle' exists only dense→rare; rare→dense always refracts. Real surfaces also polarise (Brewster) and absorb — Snell tracks direction only.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From wavefronts: in time t the incident front advances c₁t and the refracted front c₂t along the boundary; geometry gives sin i/sin r = c₁/c₂ = μ₂/μ₁. Set r = 90° for the grazing limit: sin C = μ_rarer/μ_denser = 1/μ — beyond this angle no real r satisfies Snell, so reflection takes 100%.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'State conditions' for TIR = 2 marks free: dense→rare + i > C. μ = c/v converts every speed question. Remember C_glass ≈ 42°, C_water ≈ 49°, C_diamond ≈ 24° — one line that answers many MCQs.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): Snell's law + speed of light in glass (μ = 1.5). NEB 2022 (2): TIR + its two conditions. Relation between refractive indices and lateral-shift numericals complete the set.
